The '''Solaran Academy of Linguistics''' was a scholarly institution associated with Solaran language research, script development, and terminology support.

== Source Role ==

Source material cites the academy in 1900 for work on the development of the [[Solaran Alphabet|Sunline]] writing system. That places the academy in the immediate aftermath of the 1898 alphabet adoption and connects it to the broader literacy reforms begun under the [[Education Reform Act of 1895]].

== Work ==

The academy studied Solaran grammar, dialect variation, writing systems, and the relationship between the modern [[Solaran Language]] and older [[Solra]]. It likely supported school standards, official spelling, and the adaptation of classical vocabulary into modern public usage.

Its work was more scholarly than ministerial. Where the [[Solaran Ministry of Education]] implemented curriculum and the [[Solaran Language Office]] managed usage, the academy supplied research and prestige.

== Place In Solaran Modernization ==

The academy helped make the Sunline reform appear both modern and culturally legitimate. By studying the older classical script while supporting a simpler public alphabet, it gave Solara a way to modernize without presenting literacy reform as a break from tradition.

== Canon Notes ==

The source does not yet give a firm founding date or institutional charter. This draft uses 1900 as the earliest source-attested reference, not necessarily the date of creation.
